text:
Anna Li: heads up — after yesterday's quant4b smoke we saw a weird spike in duplicate fingerprints between seedbank-v2 imports and the synth-harvest bucket. probably tokenizer/quantization aliasing but need to triage before we refresh goldset.
kevin_w: can you paste the top example pairs?
Anna Li: sure, a couple quick ones:
- seed: 'How to reset router?' 
  synth: 'how do I factory reset my router'
- seed: 'refund policy for subscription'
  synth: 'how to get refund for subscription plan'
these were 98%+ fp match after token-level truncation.
maya_r: are we using the hashed token bytes fp or a text-normalized fp?
Anna Li: hashed token bytes (fast path) — code here: 
```python
# quick fp we used in smoke
import hashlib
def fp(tokens):
    b = bytes(tokens)
    return hashlib.sha1(b).hexdigest()[:12]
```
kevin_w: aha — that approach is susceptible to tokenizer changes and quantization packing. we should run a character-normalized fallback first (cheap).
olga: labelers will start seeing lots of duplicates if we don't dedupe on import. can we do a fuzzy-jaccard step in between? even a 0.85 jaccard on word-ngrams would cut most.
simon: quick plan proposal: 1) run byte-hash fp as is (fast) 2) for collisions, compute simple normalized fp (lowercase, punctuation strip) 3) for high-collision groups, run n-gram Jaccard filter 4) only surface groups > 3 duplicates to labelers for merge.
labeler-bot: FYI — current labeler queue size for curation: 3.2k. If we push duplicate groups >3, expected surge ~600 tasks.
ops-bot: triggered job: runs/dedupe-crosscheck-2469 queued.
maya_r: for the small groups (2 items) I'd prefer auto-tag as 'possible-dup' and drop from golden candidate. big groups go to human.
kevin_w: also need to ensure fingerprinting uses the same tokenizer version across runs. Recommend pin to tokenizer v1.14 for this rollback window.
Anna Li: agreed. action items: 
- kevin: write the normalized fp script and run across S3 prefix s3://redwood-harvest/{seed,synth}-2026-03-*/ (due EOD)
- simon: add jaccard pass to pipeline, threshold 0.85, and surface groups>3 to labelers (due tomorrow morning)
- olga: update labeler instructions to skip obvious paraphrase merges and only mark canonical exemplar (due tomorrow)
- maya: hold golden refresh until dedupe results are in; also run a small quant smoke to confirm no new aliasing introduced by quant kernel change.
kevin_w: command I'll run: `python infra/tools/run_fp.py --prefix s3://redwood-harvest/merged/ --out /tmp/fps.jsonl --mode normalized`
Anna Li: sample outputs I'll paste to the thread once done, but here's one interesting failure case where tokenizer byte packing created identical bytes: `"\xf0\x9f\x98\x80"` in the middle of strings.
olga: labeler instructions draft: "If two items are near-duplicates but differ only in punctuation or stopword order, merge into the canonical form. If content differs in intent or entity, file as separate." will push in docs.
simon: on the quant side, we should run the candidate model A vs A-quant diff eval on the deduped holdout set — we might be hiding regressions otherwise. I'll add that to the rollout checklist.
maya_r: scheduling note: I'll block 1h tomorrow 10:30 for quick review.
Anna Li: thanks all. I'll post results (top 100 collision groups) when kevin's run completes.
kevin_w: started full run (job id rfp-2469). ETA ~45m. pinging when done. :hourglass: 
ops-bot: job rfp-2469 started by kevin_w at 2469123470
labeler-bot: prepped a small queue template `dup-merge-v2` for groups>3, includes instructions and sample diffs.
Anna Li: perfect — if collision clusters overlap with current goldset entries we'll mark those gold examples as frozen and skip replacement until manual review.
kevin_w: run finished. uploading sample to https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-harvest/samples/rfp-2469-top100.jsonl
Anna Li: got it, samples look noisy but actionable. I'll triage top 20 and flag 5 for potential gold conflicts.
olga: thanks — I'll prep labelers once simon wires the Jaccard pass.
simon: PR for pipeline jaccard posted: https://github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/842 — reviewers: @kevin_w @maya_r. includes unit tests and perf note (extra 0.4s per item).
maya_r: reviewing now. small perf cost but worth it.
Anna Li: closing loop: we will hold golden refresh, run quant-smoke on deduped holdout, and if no regressions, proceed with refresh next week. I'll update release notes. :white_check_mark:
kevin_w: thanks everyone.
